51242561.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant full-length human N-terminal His6-tagged WDR5 (1 to 334 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) by surface plasmon resonance analysis

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) assay was performed to test the direct interaction between the representative analogue and WDR5 and its specificity for MLL1. The SPR assay was carried out on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). Recombinant full-length human N-terminal His6-tagged WDR5 (1 to 334 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) was immobilized on a CM5 chip via amine coupling. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% P20. The analyte (DC_M4_1) was injected at concentrations of 4.76, 8.57, 15.43, 27.77, and 50.00 μM. The association time was 120 s and the dissociation time was 180 s. The data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) was calculated from the sensorgram.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. SPR curves for WDR5 binding with DC_M4_1. The concentrations of DC_M4_1 injected over the CM5 chip and was immobilized with WDR5 protein. This assay yielded Kd values of 15.8 μM for WDR5 binding with compound DC_M4_1.
original_paragraph.Results Section: According to Figure 5, DC_M4_1 completely binds to WDR5 at 120s and quickly dissociate from WDR5 at 180s, indicating that it is a reversible inhibitor. Besides, it dose-dependently and strongly binds to WDR5 with the equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) values of DC_M4_1 and DC_M5_2 are 15.8 μM and 13.8 μM. These results suggest that DC_M4_1 could be characterized as a specificity and reversible non-covalent inhibitor.
